## chok

`import "github.com/zynthara/chok/v3"` — Package chok is an opinionated toolkit for Go applications that are assembled with plain code: one strict typed configuration, an App with a predictable lifecycle, typed HTTP handlers with a runtime OpenAPI document, and error values that describe their own HTTP response.

| `func ClientIP(ctx context.Context) string` | ClientIP returns the client address, read from forwarding headers only when the direct peer is one of http.trusted_proxies. |
| `func DELETE[T, R any](r Router, pattern string, fn HandlerFunc[T, R], opts ...RouteOption)` | DELETE registers fn for DELETE pattern on r; see GET for binding. |

| `func List[T any](r Router, pattern string, l Lister[T], opts ...RouteOption)` | List registers GET pattern on r to serve pages from l: page, size, order=field:asc\|desc and every field of l.QueryFields() as an equality filter come from the query string. |

`import "github.com/zynthara/chok/v3/store"` — Package store is the typed data access of a model: CRUD with optimistic locking and soft delete, filtered and paged lists, aggregates, and an owner scope that fences every query to the caller's rows.

| ↳ `func Set(kv map[string]any) *Changes` | Set writes the given fields, named by their public names, with no optimistic lock unless the Update adds where.Version. |
| `type DuplicateError struct{ ... }` | DuplicateError is a write that a unique constraint refused. |
| `type EmptyChangesError struct{}` | EmptyChangesError is an update that changes nothing. |

## jobs

`import "github.com/zynthara/chok/v3/jobs"` — Package jobs is chok's battery for background work: periodic jobs on cron schedules, and workers that deliver, at least once and in order, the messages the application enqueues in its own transactions.

| Declaration | |
|---|---|
| `var ErrOutsideTx error = outsideTxError{}` | ErrOutsideTx is what Enqueue returns when its context does not carry a transaction of the database the jobs run on: the message must commit or roll back with the writes it describes, so an autocommit insert, or one riding another handle's transaction, is refused. |
| `func New(cfg Config, d *db.DB, opts ...Option) (*Jobs, error)` | New builds the jobs battery on d: it checks cfg and every option, then registers the tables chok_jobs_messages and chok_jobs_watermarks under the owner "jobs" (created now in migrate: auto; from its embedded SQL files in migrate: versioned). |
| `type Config struct{ ... }` | Config is the jobs section of an application's configuration: |
| `type Event struct{ ... }` | Event is one moment of a run that Observe reports: a periodic job's run, a worker's sweep of its topic or the retention cleanup's run starting, finishing or failing, or a trigger skipped while a run was in flight. |
| `type JobStats struct{ ... }` | JobStats counts the runs of a periodic job, a worker's sweeps, or the retention cleanup's runs. |
| `type Jobs struct{ ... }` | Jobs is the jobs battery: periodic jobs on cron schedules, and workers that deliver the messages Enqueue writes. |
| ↳ `func MustNew(cfg Config, d *db.DB, opts ...Option) *Jobs` | MustNew is New that panics on error. |
| `type Message struct{ ... }` | Message is an enqueued message as a worker receives it. |
| `type Option func(*options)` | Option configures New. |
| ↳ `func Logger(l *slog.Logger) Option` | Logger is where the jobs log; the default is the database handle's logger. |
| ↳ `func Observe(fn func(ev Event)) Option` | Observe calls fn at every run's start, end and failure, and at every trigger skipped because a run was in flight — of the periodic jobs, the workers' sweeps and the cleanup alike. |
| ↳ `func Periodic(name, spec string, fn func(ctx context.Context) error, overlap Overlap) Option` | Periodic runs fn on the cron schedule spec — five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), six with leading seconds, or a descriptor such as @hourly or "@every 10m" — in the machine's time zone unless spec starts with CRON_TZ=&lt;zone&gt;. |
| ↳ `func Worker(topic string, fn func(ctx context.Context, m Message) error) Option` | Worker delivers the messages enqueued under topic to fn, one at a time in (created_at, id) order, at least once: a message is redelivered after fn fails on it, and after a restart within the settle window, so fn must be idempotent — dedupe on Message.ID or on a key in the payload. |
| `type Overlap int` | Overlap says what a periodic job does when its schedule fires while its previous run is still going. |
| ↳ `const OverlapSkip Overlap = iota ...` | OverlapSkip, OverlapQueue, OverlapAllow: OverlapSkip drops the trigger: for frequent jobs, where the next trigger comes soon anyway. |
| `type Stats struct{ ... }` | Stats is a snapshot of the background work of this process. |

`import "github.com/zynthara/chok/v3/cache"` — Package cache is chok's cache battery: byte values under string keys, in a memory layer in the process, a Redis layer shared by the replicas, or both, with a circuit breaker in front of Redis, under one Config.

## choktest

`import "github.com/zynthara/chok/v3/choktest"` — Package choktest is what an application's tests need from chok: a throwaway database of the lane's dialect, a store on it, an App served in process, and a JSON client for that App.

| Declaration | |
|---|---|
| `func DB(t testing.TB, specs ...db.TableSpec) *db.DB` | DB opens a fresh database with the given tables, migrated, and closes and drops it when the test ends. |
| `func Principal(ctx context.Context, p chok.Principal) context.Context` | Principal returns ctx carrying p, for calling stores directly as an authenticated user would. |
| `func Store[T db.Modeler](t testing.TB, opts ...store.Option) *store.Store[T]` | Store returns the store of T on a fresh database holding T's table, as store.New would with opts. |
| `type Client struct{ ... }` | Client sends requests to an App in process. |
| ↳ `func App(t testing.TB, base chok.Base, setup func(app *chok.App)) *Client` | App builds an App from base — a zero Base means every default — runs setup on it to register components and routes, and runs its start phase: Starters start and every Healther must report healthy. |

## realtime

`import "github.com/zynthara/chok/v3/realtime"` — Package realtime is chok's battery for pushing events to browsers as they happen: a Hub of topics that clients subscribe to over a WebSocket or a server-sent event stream, opened with one-time tickets, resumed after a reconnect from a short replay buffer, and shared by the replicas of a deployment through Redis.

| Declaration | |
|---|---|
| `type Config struct{ ... }` | Config is the realtime section of an application's configuration: |
| `type Event struct{ ... }` | Event is one event as a client receives it: a WebSocket text frame carries one, and so does the data line of a server-sent event. |
| `type Hub struct{ ... }` | Hub is the realtime battery: the topics, the connections subscribed to them over WebSocket or server-sent events, the tickets that open them, and, with Redis, the backplane to the other replicas. |
| ↳ `func MustNew(cfg Config, opts ...Option) *Hub` | MustNew is New that panics on error. |
| ↳ `func New(cfg Config, opts ...Option) (*Hub, error)` | New builds a hub from cfg after checking cfg and every option; nothing runs until Start, and nothing is served until Mount. |
| `type Option func(*options)` | Option configures New. |
| ↳ `func Authn(mw chok.Middleware) Option` | Authn guards {Path}/ticket with mw — identity's Authn(), typically — so that a ticket carries the principal mw puts in the request, and the connection it opens acts for that user. |
| ↳ `func Authorize(fn func(ctx context.Context, topic string) error) Option` | Authorize decides which topics a connection may subscribe to: fn runs once per subscription, with a context that carries the ticket's principal (none for an anonymous ticket), and refuses the subscription by returning an error. |
| ↳ `func Logger(l *slog.Logger) Option` | Logger is where the hub logs; the default is slog.Default(). |
| ↳ `func Redis(client *goredis.Client) Option` | Redis makes the hub one of several replicas sharing client: tickets live in Redis, so any replica redeems a ticket and only once, and every Publish also reaches the other replicas' subscribers, through PUBLISH on Config.Channel. |
| `type Stats struct{ ... }` | Stats is a snapshot of a Hub: its connections and its counters since New. |

## mail

`import "github.com/zynthara/chok/v3/mail"` — Package mail is the mail battery: transactional mail — a sign-in code, a password reset, an order confirmation — sent with one value and the standard library only.

| Declaration | |
|---|---|
| `type Attachment struct{ ... }` | Attachment is a file that travels with a mail. |
| `type Config struct{ ... }` | Config is the mail section of an application's configuration: |
| `type Mailer struct{ ... }` | Mailer sends mail: m.Send(ctx, mail.Message{To: …, Template: …, Data: …}). |
| ↳ `func MustNew(cfg Config, opts ...Option) *Mailer` | MustNew is New that panics on error. |
| ↳ `func New(cfg Config, opts ...Option) (*Mailer, error)` | New builds a mailer: it checks cfg, what the transport needs and every template, and creates transport dir's directory; it does not touch the network. |
| `type Message struct{ ... }` | Message is one mail. |
| `type Option func(*options)` | Option configures New. |
| ↳ `func Logger(l *slog.Logger) Option` | Logger is where the mailer logs; the default is slog.Default(). |
| ↳ `func Sender(fn func(ctx context.Context, m *Message, raw []byte) error) Option` | Sender replaces the transport, Config.Transport and its settings included: fn gets each composed message — m as rendered, its Subject, Text and HTML filled from the template — and raw, its RFC 5322 text, ready for an HTTP API or a test to take. |
| ↳ `func Templates(fsys fs.FS) Option` | Templates gives the mails their templates: in fsys, each {name}.html is an html/template, and {name}.txt, a text/template, is its optional plain-text version, sent with it as multipart/alternative. |
| `type SMTPConfig struct{ ... }` | SMTPConfig is mail.smtp: the relay a transport smtp mail goes through, such as Resend's, Postmark's or Amazon SES's. |
